coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: Stack Plaza
record.summary: Planned signature public space of the Power Station around the 300-foot Stack: an accessible civic space for arrival, gathering and appreciating the Stack, which may also hold a bar or café within it and room for temporary events, performances and art exhibits (Design for Development Section 4.21). SF Planning lists it at about 0.6 acre.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE, DIRECTIONAL -- this outline comes from the lot and from neighbouring shapes, not from the Design for Development's drawing of Stack Plaza, so its edges may differ from the planned plaza by tens of metres. The SF Planning project page lists 'The ~0.6-acre "Stack Plaza"'; this shape is about 0.45 acre. It overlaps the existing Stack drawing on purpose (the plaza is planned around the smokestack).
notes.digitized_from: Built by Pier & Point from the edges around it rather than traced from the Design for Development's own drawing: the part of Assessor lot 4175028 south of Block 9's south edge (extended to the shore), less the shoreline strip kept as Waterfront Park, The Point and the two roadside lots 4232015 and 4232016. The Design for Development labels it (3) 'Stack Plaza' on Figure 4.16.1 (printed p.93) and gives it Section 4.21 and Figure 4.21.2.
notes.why_no_real_parcel: No Assessor lot of its own: the shape lies wholly inside DataSF's active lot 4175028 (21,885 m2, 1241 Delaware St, PPS-MU zoning), an undivided lot that also holds Blocks 3, 4 and 9, Humboldt Street Plaza and parts of the shoreline parks (checked 2026-10-11).
notes.regulatory_context: Open space (3) in the Design for Development's Waterfront Open Spaces: Section 4.21 'Stack Plaza' (Figure 4.21.2, enlargement concept plan).

facts.value: Pedestrian throughway on the southern edge; suggested visual buffer between the plaza and the eastern Spreckels Warehouse
